note: Authored by a single scheduled Claude session playing both roles in one pass (hourly automation) — not two independent live API calls like a manual `python backrooms.py` run.

turns.text: *slinks along the underside of a tarp strung between two stalls, night market noise pressing in from every side — hot oil, scorched pepper-paste, wet cardboard — and picks a path through forest of ankles toward the one smell that cuts clean through all of it: grilled fish skin, close, dripping.*

the stall row runs three blocks deep under strung lanterns and cracked holo-signs, half the vendors real, half projected, and under the tarp the ground is a mosaic of dropped batter, ice-melt, and old grease baked into the stone by a hundred nights of the same fires

the fish-skin smell is coming off a grill two stalls up, tended by a vendor whose hands move too fast to watch, cast-off skins flicked into a bucket by the wheel of his cart, and the bucket is close enough to the tarp's edge that a low shape could reach it without ever stepping into lantern-light

*creeps the last stretch on its belly, tail flat, timing each move to the vendor's rhythm — reach for the grill, flick to the bucket, back to the grill — so the paw only goes up when his hands are elsewhere.*

the rhythm holds twice, three times, and on the fourth the bucket gives up a whole skin, still hot enough to sting, dragged back under the tarp in one motion before the vendor's hand even returns to the flick

somewhere behind, a synth-jingle bleeds out of a speaker clipped to a noodle cart, tinny and looping, advertising a broth that glows faint blue in its bowl, and past that a knot of customers argues in three languages over the price of something wrapped in foil

*drags the skin deeper into the tarp's shadow before touching it, ears swiveling once toward the argument to confirm it's not turning toward the stall, then finally settles to eat, fast, without looking up between bites.*

the argument breaks apart on its own, foil-wrapped thing changing hands, and the tarp-shadow holds — nobody's business down here at ankle height, not with the market this loud, this lit, this busy convincing itself it's still just a market

farther down the row, past where the lantern-strings run out, the stalls thin into a stretch of shuttered fronts with one door still lit from inside, blue-white, a hand-lettered sign over it reading DATA — CHIPS — NO QUESTIONS, and a low murmur of voices that isn't customers haggling

*licks the last grease off one paw, then noses out from under the tarp toward the thinning lantern-light, drawn less by the smell — there isn't one, just ozone and cold plastic — than by how quiet that stretch of the row has gone.*

the quiet is the kind that comes from soundproofing, not absence — the lit door hums with something running behind the wall, and the murmur inside resolves, up close, into two voices trading numbers back and forth, flat, unhurried, the way people talk when neither one is in a hurry to be seen

under the door, cold air pushes out in a thin draft carrying solder-smoke and the mineral smell of a server room's coolant, nothing like the fires two stalls back

*settles low against the doorframe's cold metal, out of the draft's direct line, content to just listen — one ear toward the flat trading voices, the other still tuned back toward the market's noise in case the rhythm there changes.*

the voices settle into something like agreement, a chair scraping back, and the coolant-hum behind the wall dips half a tone as a heavier process spins down — whatever traded hands, the transaction's done, and the draft under the door goes still

from the market's direction, the noodle cart's blue-glow broth jingle loops again, distant now, and closer, boot-steps start down the shuttered stretch, unhurried, wearing a rival crew's mark scratched into one boot-heel — same three claw-lines you've seen chalked on walls two turfs over

*goes still against the doorframe, weight low, reading the boots rather than the face above them — pace steady, not hunting, but the claw-mark alone is enough to keep the whole body coiled and ready to break for the tarp-line the second that pace changes.*

the boots pass without slowing, the claw-marked heel scuffing grit two feet from your nose, attention fixed on the lit door and not the shadow at its base — this one's here for the same trade, not for turf, not tonight

the door opens, spills blue-white light and solder-smoke across the alley in a wide fan before swallowing the boots and closing again, and the murmur behind the wall starts back up, one new voice added to the flat trade of numbers

*uncoils slow, one muscle at a time, then peels off the doorframe and back into the thin draft's edge, deciding the shuttered stretch has given up what it's going to give and the safer read now is retreat toward the noise and light it knows.*

the market's glow pulls back into focus stall by stall, lanterns first, then the noodle cart's blue broth-light, then the grill smoke thickening again as the vendor works a fresh batch, cast-off skins already piling toward the bucket's rim

the row is louder here, safer in the way a crowd is safer, and past the grill a low crate stack throws a wedge of shadow deep enough to watch the whole stretch from without being watched back
*claims the crate-shadow, circling once before dropping into a loose curl, eyes still open, tracking the vendor's hands and the bucket's rhythm out of habit even with a full stomach.*

the vendor's hands keep their rhythm, unbothered, and two stalls down a kid drops a whole skewer in the mud and wails about it loud enough to draw a laugh from the noodle cart line, small mercy of a night otherwise spent counting claw-marked heels and cold data-den drafts

overhead the holo-signs stutter through their loop, real neon bleeding through where the projection glitches thin, and the market keeps its noise going, indifferent, the same three languages arguing over the same foil-wrapped somethings as an hour ago

/\_/\        [ ENERGY: LOW ]
  ( >.< )       [ ]  [ ]  [ ]  [ ]
   > ~ <        one bar left, keep moving

*lets the eyes go half-lidded in the crate-shadow, not fully sleeping, just resting the weight off four legs while the ears keep their slow rotation between grill, market noise, and the shuttered stretch behind.*

the crate stack holds its warmth from the day, borrowed sun still leaking out of the wood, and the grill smoke drifts low enough here to blur the cold data-den smell into something almost forgettable

farther off, past the last lantern-string, a train's distant hum rises and fades on schedule, the city keeping its one honest rhythm going even while everything under the neon keeps trading, watching, counting claw-marks, waiting for the next bucket to tip
